01 — About

I'm Mohamed Elmeslamy, a graphic designer working across branding, visual identity, and visual communication — building logos, campaigns, and cohesive design systems for coffee shops, brands, and creative projects.

Alongside my design practice, I hold an academic background in Interior Design, which sharpened the way I think about composition, proportion, materials, and space. That spatial thinking carries directly into my graphic work: the same instincts that arrange a room guide how I balance a layout, a palette, or a page.

My focus stays on the same fundamentals in both disciplines — color theory, hierarchy, and visual storytelling — applied through the language of graphic design.

02 — Selected Work

Projects

Featured Branding / Visual Identity

BUNAÉ Coffee House — Visual Identity

A complete visual identity developed for BUNAÉ Coffee House, focusing on creating a modern, warm, and cohesive visual language inspired by the atmosphere of coffee culture.

Logo Design Visual Identity Color Palette Typography Menu Design Poster Design Social Media Design Roll-Up Design Brand Mockups

Brand Concept

BUNAÉ is a vintage-inspired coffee house identity that combines classic elegance with a warm, welcoming feeling. The decorative frame and traditional typography reflect the brand's timeless character, while an earthy color palette creates a cozy, natural atmosphere.

Name & Logo Concept

BUNAÉ takes its name from "Buna," the Ethiopian word for coffee, with an accent added for a distinctive, elegant character. The logo pairs a refined emblem shape with a bold serif typeface, built for heritage, warmth, and premium quality.

Logo Variations

Four directions were explored for the mark — vintage & classic, warm & rich, bold & modern, and clean & minimal — to test how the emblem holds up across different tones.

Color Palette

A warm, natural palette running from dark coffee through coffee bean, camel, sand dune, and floral white — chosen for a timeless, premium feel.

Menu Design

The menu carries the identity into a functional piece — coffee, hot drinks, cold drinks, and baked goods laid out with the same frame and typography as the logo.

Social Media Design

A set of social posts extends the identity into everyday promotion — pairing product photography with the brand's serif voice.

Roll-Up Design

An in-store roll-up banner translates the identity to a physical, welcoming touchpoint for the coffee house.

Brand Mockups

The finished identity applied across real-world touchpoints — storefront signage, packaging, chalkboard, stationery, and wall art.

Final Presentation

The complete BUNAÉ visual identity, brought together.
